## What to build

A Pi agent spawned by `herdr-spawn --role <role>` into a folder Pi does not trust comes up ready for a brief, instead of sticking on Pi's "Trust project folder?" dialog. Serves spec `docs/specs/roles.spec.html#launch` (a pane: herdr-spawn starts Pi through pi-role).

Decision (supervisor, per #2's open question): `pi-role` passes `pi --approve` on every launch, so Pi trusts project-local files for that run only. One mechanism: pi-role already turns a role into Pi flags. No dialog is answered, nothing is written to `~/.pi/agent/trust.json`, the parent-folder option is never in play. herdr-spawn's dialog handler stays never-confirm-blindly and fail-closed; it learns to recognise Pi's trust dialog only so that one appearing anyway fails closed with the pane dump, never answered and never falsely reported clear.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every pi-role launch (pane `--json` and headless) carries `--approve`.
- [ ] herdr-spawn detects Pi's trust dialog wording; if it shows, herdr-spawn fails closed (exit 69, tab closed, pane text printed) and sends no key to it.
- [ ] Regression test under `tests/` run by `just check`, through herdr-spawn's CLI with a fake `herdr` on PATH: passes with the fix, fails without it.
- [ ] `just check` green.
- [ ] Demo: real `herdr-spawn` from this branch into a fresh git dir under `/tmp` holding a project `.agents/skills` skill reaches a ready Pi agent, no trust dialog, `~/.pi/agent/trust.json` unchanged.

## What to build

The kit repo gets CI: a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the one gate, `just check`, on every pull request and on every push to main, so a PR's merge ask can cite a real green run instead of a local one. Serves spec `docs/specs/quality.spec.html#recipe-check` (`just check` is identical for agents, git hooks and CI). One mechanism: follow the templates' existing `check` workflow pattern; CI installs only what `just check` needs and runs `just check` itself, never a copy of its steps.

- [ ] A workflow in the kit repo runs `just check` on `pull_request` and on `push` to `main` (#recipe-check).

- [ ] `just check` green locally.
- [ ] Gate proof: a throwaway commit that `just check` rejects (a deliberate em dash, caught by check-dashes) and its revert, pushed to the lane PR in turn: one red run, then green.

## What to build

`just spec-chat REPO` (kit recipe, backed by one new script on every agent PATH) runs the machine-local Spec Chat clone's installer, `scripts/install-spec-chat --agents-only --prefix REPO`, so REPO's `.agents/skills` gets Spec Chat's skill links (spec-chat-shape, spec-chat-review, repair-specs), keeps `git status` clean by ignoring exactly those links, and never creates `.claude/` or `.codex/` (ADR 0001). ## What to build

A merge ask carries every piece of evidence the owner needs, durably on the PR, and a kit command refuses an incomplete one. `octo-feather-lane verdict <PR> <head> <report file>` creates or updates the PR's one machine-readable code-review verdict comment (marker, head, verdict, findings) and prints its URL (the deterministic helper the github skill names). `octo-feather-lane merge-ask <PR> --status <status file>` reads the PR through `gh` (works under the qc judge's offline gh) and checks its body's `## Merge ask` section: it names the PR's current head; the head's required checks pass; one row per criterion the lane claims with its qc verdict, consistent with the `qc: built ...` status commit on the PR; a link to the verdict comment, which names that head and a clear verdict; the ids flipped to built equal the status file's entries carrying this PR's number; and every failed criterion is listed with its triage (or `Failed: none`). Pass prints the section, ready for `herdr-say --parent`; failure names each missing item and the fix. The supervisor's merge-ask self-check and implement-spec step 8 point to the command (ADR 0008 smoke + owed eval).

## What to build

A spec changed after its Accept fails the gate unless a logged judgement call names the change. Each spec with a status file gets a call log beside it, `docs/specs/<slug>.calls.jsonl` (one JSON call per line, in the repo, reviewable in the PR). `octo-feather-spec-status check` (inside `just check`, so in CI the merge check) diffs each spec against its status file's `accepted_commit` itself, element by `data-anchor`, and fails naming the spec and each changed anchor no non-denied call names. A removed criterion needs a call of kind `weakens`, an added one a call of kind `adds`. The calls main already owes (spec commits since each accepted commit, not covered by this lane's spec revision) are backfilled as calls so main's own gate stays green.

Spec: `docs/specs/issue-lifecycle.spec.html#gates-spec-calls`, ADR 0021.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] issue-lifecycle `acceptance-call-guard`: a spec differing from its accepted commit by an unlogged change fails `just check`, naming the spec and the change; proven by an integration test in `tests/`.
- [ ] issue-lifecycle `acceptance-call-evidence`: a call with an empty or missing evidence field fails `just check`, naming the call; integration test.
- [ ] issue-lifecycle `acceptance-lane-from-main`: a spec that differs only by changes its logged calls name passes.
- [ ] Demo path: `octo-feather-spec-status check docs/specs` on a throwaway repo with an unlogged spec edit exits non-zero naming spec and anchor; after logging a call it exits 0.

The `github` skill splits into two packaged, self-contained skills, each `.agents/skills/<name>/` with SKILL.md and a `scripts/` folder (the herdr-comms pattern): `github-pr` (branches, pull requests, merge, consent; it also holds the fake `gh` now at scripts/qc-bin/gh, which the qc sandbox and tests use from there) and `github-issues`, the GitHub tracker skill, holding the seven fixed tracker scripts (`lane-key`, `key-from-branch`, `issue-view`, `issue-create`, `issue-comment`, `issue-done`, `pr-line`), each a thin wrapper over one `gh` command, output as spec skills#tracker-scripts says. `pi-role` reads the target's `.octo-feather.toml` from the working directory and loads the tracker skill wherever a role's `skills:` line says `{tracker}`; an unknown tracker refuses the start, naming the trackers the kit has. ## What to build

Pilot tracer bullet for the factory evals. A maintainer runs `just qa` (scripts/octo-feather-qa, which it wraps, as `just qc` wraps octo-feather-qc) and one skill trigger case runs end to end: the harness copies the case's fixture into a scratch checkout, starts the case's kit role headless through `pi-role` (`pi -p --mode json`) inside the qc judge's sandbox (no Herdr reachable, no live lane state, no credential beyond the model route), reads the Pi transcript, grades the case's facts from its hidden reference expectations (here: the role read a skill's SKILL.md), and prints one PASS or FAIL line per case with the facts that decided it; the run exits non-zero when any case fails and keeps its artifacts (prompt, transcript, grading, result) per run. Case shape follows scaling-octo-engine's `evals/role-workflows/<suite>/` (cases.json, reference/expectations.json never shown to the agent, deterministic grader). A deterministic self-test checks every case's shape and that no case's task carries the facts it is graded on; `just check` runs that self-test and never the live cases. One suite, the octo-feather-qa skill-triggers suite, with two cases for one implementer skill: one should-trigger, one should-not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] quality#acceptance-qa-per-case: `just qa` prints pass or fail per case with the transcript facts behind it and exits non-zero on any failure
- [ ] quality#acceptance-qa-cases-checked: a case missing a required field, or whose task names a graded fact, fails `just check` naming the case and the field
- [ ] demo: `scripts/octo-feather-qa --suite skill-triggers` and what it shows: two cases, each PASS or FAIL with the skill-read fact from the transcript, artifacts path printed
